title: Plural of the taught -us/-ys families
summary: For both taught -us/-ys families, replace final s with -ksia/-ksiä: kysymys (“question”) → kysymyksiä.
objectives: Form the plural partitive in this bounded word family.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: A case is a word form used for a grammatical job. The dictionary form is the form used to look up a word. The partitive has several uses; it does not always mean “some”. Here you practise forming the word, so no sentence construction is required.

Both selected singular families share this plural pattern: replace final s with -ksia/-ksiä. Keep the rest of the word, including any double vowel. The different singular -sta and -tta patterns do not produce different plural endings here. This lesson forms words only; plural abstract nouns can name kinds or instances, and are not automatically suitable in every everyday sentence.
keyPoints: Learn each word with its pattern; a similar final letter does not guarantee the same stem.

steps: Replace final s with -ksiä: kysymys → kysymyksiä.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “question”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.
